accuracy.evidence: Matches DfE National Curriculum (2013) Year 5 Fractions 'recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions and convert from one form to the other and write mathematical statements > 1 as a mixed number [for example, 2/5 + 4/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5]' (used verbatim as m5) and CCSS 4.NF.B.3. Every conversion in the lab and items was checked by hand: 7/4 = 1 3/4, 11/4 = 2 3/4 (11 = 2 x 4 + 3), 3 2/5 = 17/5, 7/3 = 2 1/3, 11/6 = 1 5/6, 9/4 and 10/4 = 2 1/2 on a 0-3 line in quarters. Numeric answers use (n-n%4)/4 so they work in the browser evaluator, and the gate checked every range corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips listed by NCETM Year 5 fractions guidance and Hackenberg's work on improper fractions: 'a fraction can't be more than 1' (step 1 prediction option 'Less than 1 whole', number-line prediction 'Between 0 and 1' and its drop message), reading digits (11/4 as '1 and 1/4', 13/5 as '1 and 3/5'), adding all parts (3 2/5 as 5/5, 4 1/3 as 5/3), multiplying the wrong parts (6/5) and dropping the whole part (4 1/3 as 4/3, m9).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagimpf is built around whole bars that overflow: pieces pour past a full bar into the next one, a pile of 11 quarters is bundled four at a time, solid whole bars are cut into fifths, and a 0-3 number line in quarters takes a draggable marker. flagfrac (equivalent fractions) re-slices a single bar and never goes past 1; flagbundle groups ten ones. The 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers both conversion rules before seeing them: pouring 7 quarters shows the spill into a second bar; bundling 11 quarters ends with '2 wholes and 3 quarters left over' and only then names 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3; cutting 3 wholes makes the count 5, 10, 15 and then 17 visible before the '3 x 5 + 2 = 17' header appears. The Build step makes them produce 7/3 and 11/6 themselves.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions each carry a tempting wrong option that the next action disproves: '7 quarters: what do you get?' (Less than 1 whole), '11/4 as a mixed number?' (1 and 1/4, read from the digits), 'How many fifths are in 3 and 2/5?' (5 fifths from 3 + 2) and 'Where does 9/4 go?' (Between 0 and 1). The kit then prints 'spot on' or 'now you know why it's ...'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with shuffled buttons and ten m= messages tied to the exact wrong pick, e.g. 'Do not read the digits. 13 fifths make 2 full groups of 5 (10) with 3 left', 'Do not drop the whole part. 4 wholes are 12 thirds' and '8/8 is 8 eighths, which fill exactly 1 bar, not 8'. The Build step's Check also names the slip (added wholes and numerator, or multiplied the wrong parts).

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 3.5 against the learner limit of 6.5 and introduces numerator, denominator, improper fraction and mixed number one at a time with a picture each. Adult text scores 5.7 against 9.5, quotes the curriculum statement and explains the n/n = 1 idea in one line.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph carries one idea (fractions can pass 1; two names for one amount; improper to mixed by grouping; mixed to improper by cutting). The adult side lists the specific slips and what the lab does in order, the family tip is a concrete toast-and-plates routine, and the content gate's filler patterns all passed.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark themes (every step, after Show me) show bars two to a row with readable 1/4 labels, the stacked fraction read-out, the full 0-3 number line with whole-number labels, and the tray drop zone clear of the controls. Every drag also has a button: Add 1 quarter, Make a whole, Cut whole 1, Marker back/on, Drop here. The 4th bar in the 3 2/5 step was clipped in the first shot and was fixed by allowing 4 slots.

accessibility.evidence: The pipeline walk ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors. The canvas aria-label is updated after every action ('Marker on 9/4, which is 2 and 1/4'), feedback is read through the aria-live line, and all challenge answers are real buttons in a labelled group.
